title: Integrate password reset and deactivation with session revocation

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Credential lifecycle tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/staff_access/test_credential_lifecycle.py

verify.summary: Compacted retained final functional PASS. Current task status is done.
Compacted final lifecycle closure: current task status is done.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-008 RED: password reset or deactivation leaves at least one already authenticated disposable session usable; GREEN: each owner-controlled command updates the principal lifecycle and revokes every current session, inactive login and old sessions return generic 401, repeated deactivation is safe, and credential/token markers remain absent from command output and logs; decisive comparison: all pre-command sessions authenticate, all post-command sessions fail generically and the redacted lifecycle projection matches the contract; artifact: isolated integration output, database projection and security scan.
purpose: Complete the accepted staff credential lifecycle so revoked or changed principals cannot retain uploader access through old sessions.
success_outcome: Password reset and deactivation revoke every current browser session, inactive principals cannot authenticate, and repeated deactivation is safe without secret disclosure.
anti_goals: Do not add reactivation, self-service reset, email recovery, session administration UI or automatic credential rotation.
Do not absorb normal browser-session behavior or Photo endpoint authorization.

forbidden_scope: New staff roles or authorization policy
stop_conditions: Reset or deactivation cannot revoke all current sessions in one owner-controlled operation.
The change would require a new credential lifecycle or external identity provider.
Any secret would be echoed, persisted in plaintext or logged.

constraints: The staff_access owner performs principal mutation and session revocation without foreign business writes.
Password reset stores a new Argon2id hash and updates password_changed_at; deactivation sets active false and deactivated_at.
Existing session authentication observes reset/deactivation revocation as generic 401.
invariants: Reset and deactivation revoke all current sessions for the target user.
Repeated deactivation is safe and does not recreate or extend sessions.
No plaintext credential, token or stored hash enters command output or logs.
verification_targets: Proof starts with one task-unique disposable active principal and multiple sessions in isolated PostgreSQL/application state; each rerun cleanup removes only those sessions/principal and discards task-local captured logs, recreates the known fixture, and performs no production lifecycle operation.
Integration proof covers password reset, deactivation, repeated deactivation, session revocation, inactive login rejection and redaction.
